hero.eyebrow: Total rewards and pay governance, India
hero.title: Pay you can cost, explain and defend.
hero.lead: A plan can look fine in the deck. Then it shows up in the accounts as a number nobody worked out. We design the pay plan, cost it, and defend it with the people who build it and the people who have to sign it. A working tool sits behind every piece of work.
hero.panelTitle: Four questions, in the same room

What it still pays after the meeting.
What breaks in a bad year.

who.title: Two kinds of reader. The person who has to build the number. The person who has to sign it.
who.lead: Here is how each seat usually puts it, and what we put in front of them.

people.says: I want to pay people fairly and hire well, without my pay bill running ahead of me. I do not have an HR team to build this.
people.gives: Clean levels and Fixed CTC bands, with the cost of every move on one page.

people.says: I have to explain every pay decision to employees, to the CEO and to the committee. I cannot do that from ten spreadsheets.
people.gives: One place for the data, plain explanations on every screen, and approvals on record.

people.says: Tell me what it costs this year, what it costs later and what happens in a bad year, in numbers that tie to the accounts.
people.gives: The cash, the profit and loss and the accounting charge on one page.

people.says: I have to sign this. I want to see what was rejected, not only what is recommended, and who approved it.
people.gives: A short paper the committee can decide on, with sources, assumptions and risks.
